mainTopic: Wasting seed and arousal; women and a כהן שוטה who cannot check their own purity (נדה 13b)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a rule about where a man may hold himself, then speaks strongly about deliberately causing arousal. רב says such a man deserves נידוי, because he stirs up his own יצר הרע. רבי אמי adds that he is called an עבריין, since the יצר הרע leads a person step by step all the way to עבודה זרה. רבי אלעזר and the school of רבי ישמעאל use פסוקים to show how serious wasting seed is. A ברייתא says converts and 'those who play with children' delay the משיח, and the גמרא explains the second group as men who marry girls too young to have children. The גמרא then asks whether the משנה's 'the hand should be cut off' is a real punishment or only a curse. It tries to prove the answer from רבי טרפון, but the proof falls away. A new משנה teaches that capable women may check women who cannot check themselves, and the גמרא clarifies who is on that list. Finally, a ברייתא discusses how a כהן שוטה can stay טהור to eat תרומה, which leads to a discussion of pouches and of trousers, and a new statement of אביי that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Above the corona it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes a ruling that started just before: holding oneself from the עטרה and above is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the corona and above, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a rule that began in the previous lines. It says that touching the organ from the עטרה upward is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the rule allowed contact below the עטרה, where it is less likely to cause arousal. This line sets the limit: higher up is forbidden. That sets the stage for the next statements about the danger of arousal.

keyTerms.meaning: The corona, the rim of the organ

phrases.english: From the corona and above — it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling begun earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Contact from the עטרה and above is forbidden.

steps.title: רב: one who deliberately causes arousal deserves ostracism
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a man who deliberately brings himself to arousal should be placed in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: One who intentionally causes himself to become aroused shall be placed in excommunication.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a strong ruling. A man who deliberately makes himself aroused deserves נידוי, a formal ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is לדעת, meaning 'on purpose.' רב is not talking about something that happens by itself. He means a person who knowingly brings it about, and he gives a harsh communal punishment for it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who causes himself to become aroused
Ostracism, a formal ban from the community

phrases.english: Rav says:
One who intentionally causes himself an erection —
shall be ostracized.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where one may touch to the person who deliberately causes arousal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Deliberately causing oneself arousal deserves נידוי.

steps.title: Why not just say it is forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב gave a punishment instead of simply calling the act forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let him say simply that it is 'forbidden'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's wording. Why did he jump to נידוי instead of just saying 'it is אסור,' the way the previous line did?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous line used the plain word אסור. נידוי is much harsher, so the גמרא wants to know what makes this case serious enough to deserve a ban. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him say (a challenge to the wording)

phrases.english: And let him say it is "prohibited"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the harsh wording of רב's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's choice of נידוי rather than a plain prohibition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the act is simply forbidden, a plain 'אסור' would be enough, so why a ban?

steps.title: He stirs up the evil inclination against himself
steps.stepSummary: נידוי is fitting because such a person deliberately incites the יצר הרע against himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he incites the evil inclination upon himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this is worse than an ordinary forbidden act. The person is actively stirring up his own יצר הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not only the act itself. By arousing himself on purpose, he brings on further temptation and sin. Because he invites so much danger, a stronger response like נידוי is fitting.

phrases.english: Because he arouses the evil inclination upon himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to רב's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reason behind the harsher language
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It is just an ordinary prohibition, so a plain 'אסור' would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because he actively incites the יצר הרע against himself, נידוי is fitting.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that חז״ל treat inviting temptation as more serious than a single act.

steps.title: רבי אמי: he is called a transgressor
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says such a person is called an עבריין, because the יצר הרע leads a person step by step until he worships idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי says: He is called a transgressor, for this is the method of the evil inclination. Today it tells him 'do this,' the next day 'do this,' and the next day 'go worship idols,' and he goes and worships.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives a different description of the same person. He calls him an עבריין and explains how the יצר הרע works one small step at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יצר הרע does not start with the biggest sin. It begins with small requests, and once a person gets used to giving in, it can lead him all the way to עבודה זרה. So someone who invites his יצר הרע is on a dangerous path.

keyTerms.meaning: A transgressor, someone who habitually sins
His craft, his method of working

steps.whatToRemember: The יצר הרע works step by step. Small surrenders can lead to the gravest sins.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ami says: He is called a "transgressor,"
for this is the craft of the evil inclination:
today he says to him, "Do this,"
and the next day he says to him, "Do this,"

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמָחָר אוֹמֵר לוֹ ״לֵךְ עֲבוֹד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה״ —
phrases.english: and the next day he says to him, "Go worship idols" —
and he goes and worships.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second view on the person in רב's case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who deliberately causes arousal is called an עבריין, since giving in to the יצר הרע leads step by step to grave sin.

steps.title: Another version: he is kept out of God's presence
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבי אמי says that anyone who brings himself to impure thoughts is not let into the presence of הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבי אמי said: Anyone who brings himself to impure thoughts is not brought into the domain of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of what רבי אמי said. In this version he says such a person is kept out of God's presence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the topic is wider: not only a physical act, but bringing oneself to הרהור, impure thoughts. The result is spiritual distance from הקדוש ברוך הוא. The next step brings the proof from פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure thoughts, arousal of the mind

phrases.english: Some say, Rabbi Ami says:
Anyone who brings himself into a state of arousal —
they do not bring him in
within the boundary of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רבי אמי's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who brings himself to הרהור is kept out of God's presence.

steps.title: Proof from the word 'evil' in two verses
steps.stepSummary: The word 'רע' links the פסוק about אונן to a פסוק in תהלים saying evil cannot dwell with God.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here: 'And it was evil in the eyes of the Lord,' and it is written there: 'For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second version of רבי אמי's statement. It links two פסוקים that share the word 'רע', evil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about אונן calls his act 'רע' in God's eyes. The פסוק in תהלים says 'רע' cannot dwell with God. Putting the two together, someone who does what אונן did is kept away from God's presence.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here (the first verse in a comparison)
It is written there (the second verse being compared)
Evil shall not dwell with You

phrases.english: It is written here: "And it was evil in the eyes of the Lord,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:10, about אונן.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״כִּי לֹא אֵל חָפֵץ רֶשַׁע אָתָּה
phrases.english: and it is written there: "For You are not a God who has pleasure in wickedness;
phrases.notes: תהלים 5:5.

phrases.english: evil shall not sojourn with You."
phrases.notes: The shared word 'רע' is what connects the two פסוקים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second version of רבי אמי's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That one who brings himself to הרהור is kept out of God's presence.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 38:10 linked to תהלים 5:5 by the shared word 'רע'.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: 'Your hands are full of blood'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains the פסוק 'Your hands are full of blood' as referring to those who waste seed by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר says: What is meant by 'Your hands are full of blood'? These are those who commit adultery with the hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר reads a פסוק in ישעיהו as speaking about this sin. He shows how serious it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of hands 'full of blood,' a very harsh image. רבי אלעזר applies it to men who waste seed by hand, comparing the act to bloodshed. This shows how severe חז״ל consider it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of the verse (opens an explanation of a פסוק)
Those who commit adultery with the hand, wasting seed

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says:
What is that which is written: "Your hands are full of blood"?
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:15.

phrases.english: These are those who commit adultery with the hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מַאי דִכְתִיב יְדֵיכֶם דָּמִים מָלֵאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another statement about how severe this sin is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wasting seed by hand is compared to having hands full of blood.

steps.title: School of רבי ישמעאל: 'Do not commit adultery' includes this
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that 'לא תנאף' also forbids wasting seed, whether by hand or by foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'You shall not commit adultery' means there shall not be adultery in you, whether by hand or by foot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל that supports רבי אלעזר. It reads 'לא תנאף' from the עשרת הדברות as including this sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually 'לא תנאף' is understood as forbidding relations with a married woman. This teaching reads it more broadly as 'do not be a נואף' in any form, including wasting seed by hand or foot. It backs up רבי אלעזר's use of the word 'adultery' for this act.
steps.whatToRemember: חז״ל treat wasting seed as a very serious sin. They connect it to bloodshed and to the איסור of 'לא תנאף'.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"You shall not commit adultery" —
phrases.notes: שמות 20:13.

phrases.english: there shall not be (adultery among you) [an adulterer],
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, reads 'do not be a נואף.'

phrases.english: whether with the hand or with the foot.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: לֹא תִנְאָף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's description of this act as 'adultery'.
steps.raayaObject: That wasting seed by hand counts as a form of ניאוף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 20:13, 'לא תנאף', as read by the school of רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: Converts and those who play with children delay the Messiah
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that converts and 'those who play with children' hold back the coming of the משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Converts and those who play with children delay the Messiah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא listing two groups who hold back the משיח. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not explain either group. The גמרא will now work out what each one means and why it delays the משיח.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally, 'those who play with children.' The גמרא will define it.
They delay the coming of the משיח

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Converts and those who play with children
delay the Messiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the wasting-seed theme with a new ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Converts and 'those who play with children' delay the משיח.

steps.title: Converts are understood, but what is 'playing with children'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the converts part because of רבי חלבו, then asks what 'playing with children' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: Converts make sense, as רבי חלבו said: 'Converts are as hard for Israel as a scab.' But what does 'those who play with children' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the converts part is easy to understand from רבי חלבו's teaching. It then asks what the second group is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'בשלמא... אלא' pattern means: one part is clear, but the other part is not. The real question is the meaning of 'playing with children.'

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? What does it refer to?

phrases.english: Granted, converts
fits the view of Rabbi Chelbo,
as Rabbi Chelbo said:
"Converts are as hard for Israel as a scab,"
but those who play with children,
what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the ברייתא's terms
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What sin is meant by 'those who play with children'?

steps.title: It cannot mean relations with a male
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests משכב זכור and rejects it, because that sin carries the death penalty of stoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means relations with a male, such people are liable to stoning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible meaning and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משכב זכור is a capital sin punished by סקילה. It would be odd to describe it only as 'delaying the משיח,' so this cannot be the ברייתא's meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be tested)

phrases.english: If you say it means relations with a male,
they are liable to stoning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to step 11 and rejects it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects defining the term as משכב זכור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The punishment is far more severe than 'delaying the משיח'

steps.title: It cannot mean emitting seed through other limbs
steps.stepSummary: A second suggestion, wasting seed 'by way of limbs,' is also rejected, because such people deserve a flood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps it means by way of limbs. But they are deserving of a flood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second meaning and rejects it as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wasting seed in this way is compared to the generation of the מבול, which was destroyed for this sin. That is much worse than just delaying the משיח, so this is not the meaning either.

keyTerms.meaning: By way of limbs, meaning wasting seed without intercourse
Deserving of a flood, like the generation of the מבול

phrases.english: Rather, by way of limbs,
they are deserving of a flood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second suggestion, also rejected
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects defining the term as wasting seed through limbs
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That sin deserves a flood, far more than 'delaying the משיח'

steps.title: It means marrying girls too young to have children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'playing with children' means marrying minor girls who cannot yet bear children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means people who marry minor girls who are not yet able to bear children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer to what 'playing with children' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a marriage, so it is not as severe as the two rejected cases. But no children can come from it, so it holds back new souls from being born. That is why it 'delays the משיח.'

phrases.english: Rather, it means those who marry minor girls,
who are not able to bear children,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final answer after two rejected suggestions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Those who marry girls not yet able to bear children

steps.title: The Messiah waits until all souls are born
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי teaches that בן דוד will not come until all destined souls are born, which explains why not having children delays the משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוסי said: The son of David will not come until all the souls in the 'body' are used up, as it says: 'For the spirit that enwraps is from before Me, and the souls I have made.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer with רבי יוסי's teaching and a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משיח comes only after every destined soul is born, then a relationship that cannot produce children holds that process back. This shows why the ברייתא says these people 'delay the משיח.'

keyTerms.meaning: The משיח, descendant of King David
The souls waiting to come into bodies

steps.whatToRemember: 'Playing with children' means marrying girls who cannot yet have children. It delays the משיח because the משיח comes only once all souls are born.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yosei said:
The son of David will not come
until all the souls in the 'body' are used up,
phrases.notes: He means all the souls meant to come into the world must first be born into bodies.

phrases.english: as it is said:
"For the spirit that enwraps is from before Me,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 57:16

phrases.english: and the souls that I have made."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֵין בֶּן דָּוִד בָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 14's answer
steps.raayaObject: Why marrying girls too young for children delays the משיח

steps.title: Is cutting off the hand a real law or only a curse?
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה's words 'among men, it should be cut off,' the גמרא asks whether this is a real court punishment, like רב הונא cutting off a hand, or just a curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Among men, it should be cut off.' It was asked: Is this a law or a curse? Is it a law, like the case where רב הונא cut off a hand, or is it a curse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase in the משנה and raises a question about it. The next steps try to answer it from a ברייתא of רבי טרפון, but that proof is taken apart in steps 19–20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a man's hand that keeps checking itself 'should be cut off.' The question is whether a court actually does this, as רב הונא did in another case, or whether it is only strong language of condemnation.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before the Sages
A real law to be carried out

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא's case is a different case (hitting another person). The גמרא brings it only to show that the same wording was once carried out in practice.

phrases.english: Among men, it should be cut off.
phrases.notes: Back to our משנה: a man's hand that keeps checking itself should be cut off.

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
Did we learn a law, or did we learn a curse?
Did we learn a law,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא קַץ יְדָא,
phrases.english: like the case where Rav Huna cut off a hand,
phrases.notes: רב הונא cut off the hand of someone who struck others, where the same 'cut off' wording is used.

phrases.english: or did we learn a curse?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּאֲנָשִׁים תִּקָּצֵץ. אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: דִּינָא תְּנַן אוֹ לָטוּתָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's text to open a new question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the משנה's 'cut off the hand' a real court penalty or only a curse?

steps.title: רבי טרפון's teaching about cutting off the hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי טרפון says a hand that touches the organ should be cut off on the navel, and the Rabbis argue with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a ברייתא. רבי טרפון says: if a hand goes to the organ, the hand should be cut off on the navel. They asked: if a thorn is stuck in his belly, may he not take it out? He said: No. They said: but his belly will split open! He said: better his belly split open than he go down to the pit of destruction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question from Step 16: is 'cut off' a real punishment or just a curse? This step only quotes the source. The next step will show how it is supposed to prove the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון uses the same harsh language as our משנה: the hand 'should be cut off.' The Rabbis' objection about the belly splitting open is the key detail. It sounds like they are picturing an actual knife cutting near the belly.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Tarfon says:
A hand to the organ —
phrases.notes: אמה here means the male organ.

phrases.english: his hand should be cut off upon his navel.
They said to him:
If a thorn got stuck in his belly,
should he not remove it?!
He said to them: No.
But won't his belly be split open!
He said to them:
Better that his belly be split open,
and let him not go down to the pit of destruction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question raised in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: Whether 'cut off' is a real court punishment (דינא) or only a curse (לטותא).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי טרפון and his exchange with the Rabbis.

steps.title: The split belly only makes sense if it is a real punishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the proof. The worry 'his belly will split open' fits a real cutting, but makes no sense if it is only a curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we learned a real law, that is why they said 'his belly will split open.' But if you say we learned only a curse, what does 'his belly will split open' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how the ברייתא proves that 'cut off' is a real court punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hand is truly cut off while it rests on the navel, the knife could slice the belly. So the Rabbis' objection fits a real punishment. A mere curse involves no knife, so the belly worry would mean nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense, granted (this view fits well)
a real law, an actual punishment

phrases.english: Granted, if you say we learned a real law,
that is why they said:
'But won't his belly be split open,'
but if you say we learned only a curse,
what is 'his belly will be split open'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That 'cut off' is a real punishment (דינא).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Rabbis' words 'won't his belly be split open,' which assume real cutting.

steps.title: Even a real punishment would not need to be on the navel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Even if it is a real punishment, why cut the hand off on the navel? Just cut it off somewhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what, then? That we learned a real law? Then isn't it enough to cut it off not on his navel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. Reading it as a real punishment does not fit the ברייתא well either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a court really cuts off the hand, it would not do so on the belly, where cutting is dangerous. So the 'split belly' detail is strange under the real-punishment reading too. The proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: but what, then? (the other reading has its own problem)

phrases.english: But what, then? That we learned a real law?
Isn't it enough to do it not on his navel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the ברייתא shows 'cut off' is a real punishment.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A real punishment would not need to be carried out on the navel. So the 'split belly' worry does not really fit that reading either.

steps.title: A new reading of רבי טרפון's words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. Anyone who puts his hand below his navel deserves to have it cut off. The 'split belly' refers to a thorn he is not allowed to take out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what רבי טרפון means: whoever puts his hand below his navel, it should be cut off. They said to him: if a thorn is stuck in his belly, may he not take it out? He said: No. They said: but his belly will split open! He said: better his belly split open than he go down to the pit of destruction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי טרפון a different way. 'On the navel' now describes where the forbidden act happens, not where the cutting happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden zone is anywhere below the navel. The 'split belly' now comes from a thorn left inside, because he may not reach down to remove it. With this reading, the ברייתא no longer proves whether 'cut off' is a real punishment or a curse.

keyTerms.meaning: one who puts his hand in

steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון's teaching is reread. Putting a hand below the navel deserves cutting off, and the 'split belly' comes from a thorn he may not remove. The proof from Step 18 is gone.
steps.confusionAlert: In this reading the knife never touches the belly. The danger to the belly comes from the thorn left inside.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what Rabbi Tarfon is saying:
Anyone who puts his hand below his navel —
it should be cut off.
They said to Rabbi Tarfon:

phrases.aramaic: יָשַׁב לוֹ קוֹץ בִּכְרֵיסוֹ לֹא יִטְּלֶנּוּ?!
phrases.english: If a thorn got stuck in his belly, should he not remove it?!
He said to them: No.
But won't his belly be split open!
phrases.notes: Now this means the thorn left inside will tear his belly. It is no longer about a knife.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Better that his belly be split open,
and let him not go down to the pit of destruction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the difficulty from Step 19 by rereading the ברייתא, which also removes the proof.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Upon his navel' was where the hand would be cut, and the split belly came from the cutting.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Below the navel' is where the forbidden act happens, and the split belly comes from a thorn he may not remove.

steps.title: New משנה: women who cannot check themselves
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that a deaf, mentally incompetent, blind, or insane woman can have capable friends prepare her, and then she may eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A deaf woman, a mentally incompetent woman, a blind woman, or a woman who lost her mind: if they have capable women, those women prepare them, and they may eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It covers women who cannot reliably check their own purity status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These women cannot do the checks themselves. Capable women may do it for them, and then they are allowed to eat תרומה. This opens a new topic for the גמרא to discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: the holy portion given to the כהן

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A deaf woman, and a mentally incompetent woman,
and a blind woman, and one whose mind became deranged —
if they have capable women,
those women prepare them,
phrases.notes: They get them ready to be pure by checking them.

phrases.english: and they may eat תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous sugya ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women who cannot check themselves may be prepared by capable women and then eat תרומה.

steps.title: Why can't a deaf woman examine herself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a deaf woman needs help, since a ברייתא tells of a deaf woman who was an expert in checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: A deaf woman? Let her examine herself! As it is taught: רבי said, there was a deaf woman in our neighborhood. Not only did she examine herself, but her friends would see stains and show them to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by challenging the משנה's first case, the deaf woman. Why should she need other women to check her?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being deaf does not stop a woman from looking at a cloth. The ברייתא proves this: רבי knew a deaf woman so skilled that other women brought their stains to her. So why does the משנה treat a deaf woman as unable to check herself?

keyTerms.meaning: They show to her (to get her ruling)

phrases.english: GEMARA
A deaf woman?
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 21, which said capable friends must prepare her.

phrases.english: Let her examine herself!
As it is taught: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: There was a deaf woman in our neighborhood
Not only did she examine herself,
but her friends would see and show her!
phrases.notes: When her friends found stains and weren't sure about them, they brought them to her to decide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first case in the new משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a deaf woman needs friends to prepare her
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows a deaf woman can be fully skilled at checking, even for others

steps.title: The משנה means a woman who can neither hear nor speak
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a woman who speaks but cannot hear. The משנה is about one who can neither speak nor hear.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, she speaks but does not hear. Here, she neither speaks nor hears. As we learned: the deaf person the חכמים speak about everywhere is one who neither hears nor speaks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sources describe two different kinds of deaf women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who can speak but not hear is fully capable, like the woman in רבי's neighborhood. The משנה's חרשת is a deaf-mute, who is treated as not capable in halacha. The גמרא supports this with a משנה: whenever the חכמים say חרש, they mean someone who can neither hear nor speak.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here (the other source vs. our source)
She speaks but does not hear
Everywhere (in every place the term appears)

steps.whyThisMatters: This defines the term חרש across the whole Talmud: unless it says otherwise, it means a deaf-mute.

phrases.english: There, it is about one who speaks but does not hear;
here, it is about one who neither speaks nor hears.
As we learned in a משנה:
phrases.notes: This is תרומות 1:2.

phrases.english: The deaf person the Sages spoke of everywhere
is one who neither hears nor speaks.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם — בִּמְדַבֶּרֶת וְאֵינָהּ שׁוֹמַעַת, הָכָא — בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ מְדַבֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (two kinds of deaf women)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any deaf woman can check herself, so the משנה seems wrong
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's חרשת is a deaf-mute, who is not considered capable; a speaking deaf woman can check herself

steps.title: Why can't a blind woman check and show a friend?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a blind woman needs help. She can check herself and then show the cloth to a friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: A blind woman? Let her examine herself and show it to her friend!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the next case in the משנה, the blind woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blind woman cannot see the cloth, but she can still do the checking. Then a friend can look at it for her. So she does not seem to need others to prepare her.

keyTerms.meaning: She should show it to her friend

phrases.english: A blind woman?
Let her examine herself
and show it to her friend!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַסּוֹמָא — אִיהִי תִּבְדּוֹק לְנַפְשַׁהּ, וְתַיחְזֵי לַחֲבִירְתַּהּ!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of challenge as step 22, now aimed at the blind woman
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's inclusion of a blind woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She can do the check herself and have a friend look at the cloth

steps.title: The blind woman does not belong in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the word 'blind' should not be in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: 'Blind' is not part of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by removing the blind woman from the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not look for a special kind of blind woman. It agrees the challenge is right and says the correct wording of the משנה never listed her. So a blind woman checks herself and shows a friend.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not part of the משנה (take it out of the text)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a blind woman needs others to prepare her. The conclusion is that she was never meant to be on the list.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
'Blind' is not part of the mishna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 by changing the משנה's wording
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says a blind woman needs others to prepare her
steps.terutzMaskana: The blind woman is not in the correct text; she can check herself

steps.title: Isn't a woman who lost her sanity the same as a שוטה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה lists a woman who lost her sanity, when it already listed the שוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who lost her sanity? That is the same as a שוטה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last case in the list as a repeat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already has a שוטה, a woman who is not mentally capable. A woman who 'lost her mind' sounds like the same person. So why list her twice?

keyTerms.meaning: Her mind became confused (she lost her sanity)

phrases.english: And a woman who lost her sanity?
That is the same as an imbecile!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third challenge to a case in the משנה's list
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה listing both שוטה and שנטרפה דעתה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two cases seem identical, so one is extra

steps.title: She lost her sanity because of illness
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means a woman whose mind was confused by an illness, which is different from a שוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means one who lost her sanity because of illness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this is a different case from a שוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוטה is mentally incompetent in an ongoing way. This woman is normally fine, but a sickness confused her mind. Since she is a separate case, the משנה needs to list her too.
steps.whatToRemember: Of the משנה's list, the deaf woman means a deaf-mute and the blind woman is removed. The woman who lost her sanity is one whose mind was confused by illness, not a regular שוטה.

phrases.english: One who lost her sanity because of illness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 by showing the two cases differ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (different cause of the condition)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שנטרפה דעתה is just another name for a שוטה
steps.terutzMaskana: שנטרפה דעתה is a woman whose mind was confused by illness, a separate category

steps.title: A ברייתא: How a Mentally Incompetent Priest Becomes Pure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a כהן שוטה is immersed by others, fed תרומה in the evening, and watched so he does not sleep. If he slept he is טמא; if not, he is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A priest who is a שוטה: they immerse him, and they let him eat תרומה in the evening, and they watch him so that he does not sleep. If he slept, he is impure. If he did not sleep, he is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a כהן שוטה, a priest who cannot look after himself, and explains how others help him become טהור and eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא person who immerses must wait until nightfall before he may eat תרומה. A normal person can watch himself during that time, but a שוטה cannot. So others watch him, because if he sleeps he might have a seminal emission without knowing it and become טמא again.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest who is not mentally competent
They immerse him in a מקוה
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן, which may only be eaten in purity
In the evening, after nightfall, when the immersed person becomes fully טהור
They guard or watch over him

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: A priest who is a שוטה —
They immerse him,
and they feed him תרומה in the evening,
and they watch him so that he does not sleep.
If he slept, he is impure,
if he did not sleep, he is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After discussing the שוטה in the משנה, the גמרא brings another ברייתא about the practical laws of a שוטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן שוטה is immersed by others and watched until evening so he does not sleep. If he slept he is טמא; if not, he is טהור and may eat תרומה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק suggests a leather pouch
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says a different method can be used: make a leather pouch for the כהן שוטה so that any emission can be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says: They make a leather pouch for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק offers another way to handle the כהן שוטה: put a leather pouch on him, then check it before he eats תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of relying on keeping him awake, the pouch would catch any emission, so people could check whether he became טמא. This is a different method from the one the חכמים gave in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok says:
They make him a leather pouch.
phrases.notes: The pouch is placed on his body to catch any emission, so it can be checked before he eats.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר: עוֹשִׂין לוֹ כִּיס שֶׁל עוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second method, different from watching him so he does not sleep.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leather pouch is made for the כהן שוטה so that any emission can be detected.

steps.title: The Sages Object: Leather Causes Warmth
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים object that a leather pouch is even worse, because it warms him and makes an emission more likely.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: All the more so, since it brings about warmth!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's suggestion. They say the leather pouch would make things worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leather keeps the body warm, and that warmth could itself cause an emission. So the pouch does not prevent the problem. It makes the problem more likely, and he will become טמא all the more.

phrases.english: They said to him: All the more so,
since it brings about warmth!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁמֵּבִיא לִידֵי חִימּוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the leather pouch suggested in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's leather pouch method
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leather causes warmth, and warmth causes emissions, so the pouch increases the very טומאה it is meant to detect.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר pushes back: then the שוטה has no fix
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק answers that according to the חכמים, a שוטה would have no way at all to eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: According to your words, a שוטה has no remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק defends his idea by challenging the חכמים back. He says their approach leaves the שוטה with no solution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He seems to feel that just watching a שוטה is not reliable enough. So if the pouch is also rejected, nothing is left. He is arguing that some method must be allowed, and the pouch is the best available.

keyTerms.meaning: According to your words or view
A remedy, a way to fix the problem

phrases.english: He said to them: According to your words,
a שוטה has no remedy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: לְדִבְרֵיכֶם, שׁוֹטֶה אֵין לוֹ תַּקָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the objection by turning the challenge back on the חכמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's rejection of the pouch
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the pouch is rejected, the חכמים leave the שוטה with no workable way to become טהור and eat תרומה.

steps.title: The Sages Reply: Our Way Works, Yours Can Hide a Tiny Drop
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that their method does work: watch whether he slept. They add that the pouch is unreliable, because a drop as small as a mustard seed could soak into it unnoticed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: According to our words, if he slept he is impure, and if he did not sleep he is pure. According to your words, perhaps he will see a drop as small as a mustard seed, and it will be absorbed in the pouch!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים defend their view. They show that the שוטה does have a fix, and they add a second problem with the pouch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their method gives a clear test: did he sleep or not? With a leather pouch, a tiny drop could soak into the leather and never be noticed, so he might eat תרומה while טמא. The pouch could actually lead to a mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: According to our words or view
A drop the size of a mustard seed, meaning a tiny amount
And it will be absorbed or swallowed up

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים rely on watching that the שוטה stays awake. A leather pouch is rejected because it causes warmth and can hide a tiny drop.

phrases.english: They said to him: According to our words —
if he slept, he is impure; if he did not sleep, he is pure;
according to your words — perhaps he will see
phrases.notes: "See" here means he will have an emission.

phrases.english: a drop like a mustard seed,
and it will be absorbed in the pouch!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לִדְבָרֵינוּ — יָשַׁן טָמֵא, לֹא יָשַׁן טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's claim that the שוטה has no remedy.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the challenged view does have a working method, and adds a further flaw in the opposing method
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the pouch, there is no way to know if the שוטה is טהור.
steps.terutzMaskana: Watching whether he slept is a reliable test. The leather pouch could absorb a tiny drop and hide the טומאה.

steps.title: A Teaching in the Name of רבי אלעזר: A Metal Pouch
steps.stepSummary: A teaching in the name of רבי אלעזר says to make a metal pouch for the כהן שוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי אלעזר: They make him a metal pouch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more opinion: use a pouch made of metal instead of leather.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A metal pouch avoids both problems the חכמים raised. Metal does not cause warmth the way leather does, and a drop would not soak into it, so any emission could be seen.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opinion keeps רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's idea of a pouch, but answers both objections of the חכמים by changing the material.

phrases.english: It was taught: In the name of Rabbi Elazar they said:
They make him a metal pouch.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמְרוּ: עוֹשִׂין לוֹ כִּיס שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a pouch method that avoids the warmth and absorption problems raised against the leather pouch.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A metal pouch is made for the כהן שוטה, which neither warms him nor absorbs a drop.

steps.title: The metal pouch means copper
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the metal pouch from step 33 means a copper pouch. He backs this up with רבי יהודה's rule that hyssop stems are treated as if they were copper.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: it means a copper pouch. This matches the teaching where רבי יהודה says: we treat those hyssop stems as if they were made of copper.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is explaining what kind of 'metal' pouch the teaching in step 33 meant: copper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים worried that a leather pouch could soak up a tiny drop, so nobody would see it. Copper soaks up nothing, so any drop stays visible. רבי יהודה's rule shows that copper is the standard example of something that absorbs nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Copper. A metal that does not soak up liquid.
Hyssop, the plant used to sprinkle the purifying water.
We view it as if. Treating something as though it had a certain quality.

phrases.english: Abaye said: And of copper,
phrases.notes: He is explaining the 'metal pouch' from the last teaching.

phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
we view those hyssop stems
as if they were of copper.
phrases.notes: In other words, we treat the stems as soaking up none of the sprinkling water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word 'metal' in step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pouch for a כהן שוטה should be copper, which absorbs nothing, so any emission is visible.

steps.title: רב פפא: so trousers should be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא draws a conclusion from the חכמים: a pouch warms the body, so trousers should be forbidden for the same reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: learn from this that trousers are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא takes the reason the חכמים gave against a pouch (it warms the body) and applies it to trousers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 30, the חכמים said a pouch is worse because it warms the body and makes an emission more likely. If that is true, close-fitting trousers would do the same thing, so they should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. A conclusion drawn from an earlier statement.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
learn from this that trousers are forbidden,
phrases.notes: The 'this' is the חכמים' point that a pouch warms the body. Trousers would warm it too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a side discussion built on the reasoning from step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since warming causes emissions, trousers should be forbidden.

steps.title: But the Torah commands trousers for כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: the תורה itself tells the כהנים to wear linen trousers.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And make for them linen trousers to cover the flesh of their nakedness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how trousers could be forbidden when the תורה commands the כהנים to wear them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If trousers caused emissions and were forbidden, the תורה would not order them as part of the כהן's clothing. This פסוק seems to disprove רב פפא's conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? Introduces a challenge from a פסוק.
Linen trousers, one of the clothes of the כהנים.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"And make for them linen trousers
phrases.notes: שמות 28:42

phrases.english: to cover the flesh of nakedness"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's conclusion in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that trousers are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה commands the כהנים to wear trousers, so trousers cannot be forbidden.

steps.title: The כהנים' trousers were built differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא describing the כהנים' trousers. They were like riders' pants, went from the waist to the thighs, had laces, and had no openings in front or back.
steps.simpleTranslation: That case is different, as it is taught: What were the כהנים' trousers like? Like the riding pants of horsemen. On top they reached the waist and on the bottom the thighs. They had laces, and they had no opening in the back or in the front.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the כהנים' trousers were a special kind, so they do not disprove רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that the כהנים' trousers were built in their own way. They had laces and no opening in the back or the front. So the תורה's command was about this special garment, and רב פפא's concern about ordinary trousers still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Laces or straps used to tie the garment.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say all trousers are fine. It only says the כהנים' trousers were a special design, so they are different from ordinary ones.
steps.whatToRemember: The command for כהנים to wear trousers does not disprove רב פפא, because their trousers had a special design.

phrases.english: That one is as it is taught:
phrases.notes: 'That one' means the כהנים' trousers from the פסוק. They are a special case.

phrases.english: The trousers of the priests, what are they like?
Like a kind of riding pants of horsemen,
above, up to the waist,
below, down to the thighs,
and they have laces,
and they have no opening in the back
and no opening in the front.
